title: Sublinear-round clique detection in CONGEST
formal: Historical question, resolved affirmatively: for every fixed integer p≥4, can an n-node network detect a copy of Kₚ in o(n) synchronous CONGEST rounds, with success probability at least 2/3 on every input graph? In particular, can K₄ be detected in sublinear rounds? The later listing theorem gives Õ(n^{1−2/p}) rounds and therefore answers both questions. For p=4, the resulting Õ(√n) bound matches the original Ω(√n/log n) detection lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors.
context:
The 2018 paper gave a nontrivial lower bound but left a gap to the linear-round upper bound. Its conclusion singled out K₄ as a test case for whether even fixed-size clique detection might require nearly linear communication rounds.

The SODA 2021 result lists every fixed-size clique in Õ(n^{1−2/p}) rounds in CONGEST itself. Since some node learns each clique, this gives the detection output required by the original paper without a network-wide announcement.

PODC 2022 gives deterministic listing in n^{1−2/p+o(1)} rounds for every fixed p≥3. This also yields sublinear deterministic detection. Its n^{o(1)} overhead is a different precision from the randomized polylogarithmic overhead.

The congested-clique model permits every pair of nodes to communicate directly each round. The resolving upper bound operates on the actual edges of G in CONGEST. Equality of listing complexities between these models is an additional result, not an assumption used to reinterpret this card.
why: Locates the bandwidth cost of finding a basic dense pattern when processors communicate only along the input graph. The historical K₄ case now has matching upper and lower exponents; the broader fixed-clique sublinearity question is also answered.
status_note: Read the original local detection convention and concluding K₄ question. Matched the SODA 2021 CONGEST listing theorem to that task and checked the later PODC 2022 deterministic theorem in their full preprints and publication records. The resolution is for each fixed p; it does not give a uniform sublinear guarantee for growing clique size or classify detection for every p via listing lower bounds. No independent proof audit.

sentences: Network processors seek a fixed-size clique while sending only logarithmically many bits per edge per round.
The original question asked whether sublinear rounds suffice, especially for K₄.
A later theorem lists all fixed p-cliques in Õ(n^{1−2/p}) rounds and therefore resolves detection affirmatively.
For K₄ this matches the known lower bound up to logarithmic factors.
A 2022 theorem also gives deterministic sublinear algorithms; growing clique size and global announcements are different requirements.

references.title: Detecting Cliques in CONGEST Networks
references.locator: Unresolved-question passage on page 14; PDF page 14

definitions: The input is a finite simple undirected graph G=(V,E), |V|=n. Each vertex is a processor and each edge is a bidirectional communication link. Initially a node knows n, the fixed p, its own unique identifier and its neighbors’ identifiers; identifiers use O(log₂(n+2)) bits. The same algorithm is used at all nodes, with these local inputs, and for all graph sizes. Each round permits unlimited local computation and one O(log₂(n+2))-bit message in each direction on each incident edge; different edges may carry different messages. There is no direct communication between nonadjacent nodes. The protocol may use independent private random bits. Time counts synchronous rounds, not local computation, output length or aggregate messages. Each node outputs a bit. If G contains p distinct pairwise adjacent vertices, at least one node must output 1 with probability at least 2/3; otherwise all nodes must output 0 with probability at least 2/3. No designated node or every-node global verdict is required. The probability is over all algorithmic coins for the fixed graph and identifiers. Disconnected graphs are allowed. The round bound can be taken as a deterministic cutoff, counting overruns as failure. A sublinear bound Tₚ(n) satisfies Tₚ(n)/n→0 as n→∞ with p fixed. Õ suppresses a fixed power of log(n+2), with constants allowed to depend on p. Listing means every Kₚ is output as a tuple of identifiers by at least one node, with no false tuples; a node need not belong to the clique it outputs. Such listing implies the required local detection. The fixed-p limit is essential: no bound uniformly sublinear for p growing with n is asserted.
answer_criterion: The affirmative resolution supplies the local detection algorithm and proves its success and o(n) round bound for each fixed p≥4. The SODA 2021 theorem solves the stronger listing task in Õ(n^{1−2/p}) rounds with high probability. Its p=4 case also gives a matching detection classification up to polylogarithmic factors. Listing lower bounds for p>4 are not automatically lower bounds for detection.
